observations: Explosive vocabulary is taught on the first screen (Nitro, Aku, TNT in one row).
On ice, sliding is the crate attack; one TNT among slide targets punishes blind sliding.
Teach then twist: arrow + floating striped (S1-b) returns with an off-screen ! above it (S4-f); the bonus rehearses the head-butt that S3-c needs.
Both remote switches need backtracking and both are outside the default camera view (behind the arrival point; above the screen top).
Outline boxes placed before their switch (S4-e) are a visible promise; the first outline set (S3-c) has its switch beside it.
Checkpoints sit right after timed hazards or at the bottom of the free-fall.
The big payout (the wall) is late and guarded by ice momentum plus a penguin.
The only main 1UP is behind the hardest hidden switch.
The optional red-gem course does not add to the box total.

geometryObservations: Mode changes happen at one-way transitions (lift, free-fall shaft), and each camera mode has its own geometry grammar: into-screen sections are wide walled floors and ice fields (≈5–8 u); side-scroll sections are separate ledges (≈2–12 u) with ≈2 u gaps and crushers.

Ice escalates in four steps: a walled field with one TNT, where nothing can fall (P-S1-d) → a field with Nitro pairs, where contact kills (P-S1-e) → narrow icy bonus ledges, where sliding off is a fall (P-B-a) → ice in front of an enemy (P-S4-b).

Every crusher is followed at once by a demand — drop-pillar 1 → gap → occupied landing; drop-pillar 2 → checkpoint; log smashers → gap → penguin — so the reward for timing is flow, never a rest on the far side.
Small landings are occupied: seals and penguins wait on ≈2–4 u ledges after gaps (G-S2-a, G-S3-a, G-S3-c). F2 POINT11 names the counter — spin in the air before landing.

The two enemy kinds complement each other: penguins are timing enemies (attack when the spin stops; the slide also works), seals are group enemies (hit the first and all die) that double as bounce steps.
The twin log smashers move in unison and leave a pocket between them, so the gate accepts both a single dash and two half-dashes (O-S3-a).
The bonus entrance is a hole: the one gap meant to be fallen into is marked by a floating ? and guarded by a Nitro on its take-off edge (G-S3-b, O-S3-b).
The outline staircase floats over floor, not over a pit (F2 POINT10 screenshot): the guide's safe method (break from below) works because there is floor; climbing on top is the risky option.
S4 is a chain of cliff ledges joined by narrow plank bridges (G-S4-a); enemies, crates and arrows sit on the ledges and the bridges are pure chokes.
Vertical progress in S4 uses steel arrows as stairs (P-S4-d), then hides a switch above the camera frame (P-S4-e): the vertical framing limit is used as a design tool.
The free-fall shaft makes S4 a no-return section, so the only backward content (the green !) is placed directly behind the arrival point.
Checkpoints sit at transitions: the lift top (C1), right after drop-pillar 2 (C2) and the shaft bottom (C3).
geometryTransfer: Ice escalation with `slip` floors: (a) a walled 8 × 8 m slip field holding crates and one TNT; (b) a 6 m-wide slip approach with two staggered Nitro pairs ending at a `mover` lift (axis y) as a forced stop; (c) 3 m icy ledges with 2–3 m gaps in a side room; (d) a slip strip whose end, 1–2 m past a crate wall, holds an enemy.

Crusher → demand: a `crusher` over a 2–3 m raised block, then within 3 m a 2–2.5 m gap (well inside the 5.6 m running jump) onto a 3–4 m ledge holding a `grunt` with range ≤1 m, so neither the crusher block nor the landing is a place to stop; put the checkpoint straight after the second crusher.
Twin crushers in phase: two `crusher`s with the same cycle and phase, 2.5–3 m apart, leaving a ≥1.5 m pocket between them — one dash or two half-dashes both work.
Occupied pillar landing: a 2.3 m-wide pillar `platform` after a 2.5 m gap with an enemy on it (range ≤0.5 m); the counter is our air spin (0.3 s, +0.8 m reach) before touchdown, as in POINT11.

Marked drop-in bonus: in a side-scroll run (`zone` dir E), a 2.5 m hole between two ledges with a floating marker above it and a `returnportal` (airOnly) inside as the bonus entrance; one Nitro on the take-off edge.

Ledge-and-bridge cliff for a late section: 6–10 m ledges joined by 2 m-wide, 3–5 m-long bridges (`woodpath` or narrow `platform`), with enemies and crates only on the ledges; steel arrows as stairs to ledges 2.3–3.5 m higher (arrow apex 3.77 m above its lid).
